summary.headline: Modi Naturals H1 FY27 revenue rose 19.3% to INR361.9 crore, but Q2 EBITDA margin was 9.1% as input costs outran selling prices; FY27 guidance reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 38.9% YoY to INR204.9 crore and EBITDA rose 23.2% to INR18.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 9.1% and PAT up 9.4% to INR11 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was INR361.9 crore (+19.3%), EBITDA INR40.8 crore (+25.1%, margin 11.3%) and PAT INR23.5 crore (+14.4%). Management attributed Q2 margin pressure to a sharp rise in edible oil and grain prices that outpaced selling price increases, and said input costs are now showing signs of normalisation. The ethanol expansion from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD is complete, and management reaffirmed FY27 guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Net working capital cycle (as on 30 Sep)

segments.name: Consumer division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR87.4 crore and EBITDA INR4.9 crore (about 5.6% margin). Management said Q2 was an aberration and normal margin is 8-9%; an analyst noted quarterly sales have been stuck at INR45-50 crore.

segments.name: Bulk division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR80.8 crore and EBITDA INR0.7 crore. Q2 growth came from higher realisations; management expects realisations to moderate as commodity prices correct. Long-term EBITDA margin cited at 5-8%.

segments.name: Ethanol division
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR193.7 crore and EBITDA INR34.9 crore (about 18% margin). Capacity expanded to 600 KLPD; orders of about INR494 crore secured; new ESY order of 7.8 crore litres worth about INR500 crore (about INR600 crore with by-products). Long-term EBITDA margin cited at 12-15%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR925-965 crore reiterated; H1 delivered INR362 crore, so H2 must carry the balance, and management said H2 is typically heavier.
Analyst framing: FY27 EBITDA of about INR105 crore and PAT of INR66-70 crore imply H2 about 1.5x H1 levels; management said it remains confident.
Ethanol cost environment expected to improve in coming quarters as grain prices moderate; management pointed to a higher share of FCI rice-based ethanol with fixed price and margin structures.
Consumer input costs expected to normalise in about another quarter; sequential improvement already seen in Q3.
Management expects new consumer launches (snacking, grocery, ready-to-eat popcorn under PIPO, high-protein) within the next two to three months, under the Oleev sub-brands.
capex_capacity: Ethanol capacity expanded from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD; expanded capacities fully operational from about August 2026.
Ethanol capex for the expansion is broadly about INR300 crore, per management; exact figures to be shared later.
Ethanol order of 7.8 crore litres for ESY starting 1 November 2026 to 30 October 2027, under the cycle 1 tender; management said more orders are expected in later cycles (C2, C3).
Second ethanol facility has started with new commissioning completed, per an analyst's remark on the call.
Permissions secured for ethanol-based consumer products, but no launch timeline given.
demand_pricing: Management said FMCG demand is gradually recovering, but edible oil and packaging input costs pressured margins in Q2.
Olive oil prices have fallen over recent quarters, weighing on consumer top line; food category distribution is growing.
Ethanol by-products (DDGS) contribute 18-20% of ethanol revenue at current prices; a high-nutrition DDGS is in production at higher realisation.
Government permission for E85 and E100 in flex-fuel vehicles is expected to add long-term ethanol demand; grain-based feedstock (maize, rice) emphasised for FY27.
Analyst noted OMCs cut maize ethanol prices by about INR3 per litre; management said FCI rice ethanol fixed pricing reduces dependence on maize.

qa_highlights.question: Why has consumer business revenue stagnated at INR150-180 crore over five years, and what would drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat top line mainly to lower olive oil prices, and said food category distribution gains should reflect in upcoming quarters. An analyst asked for volume disclosure from next quarter; management agreed.

qa_highlights.question: Is ethanol Q2 revenue below expectations, and will Q3 and Q4 be even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the expansion was fully operational around August, so Q2 captured part of it and Q3 will reflect it fully. No slippage in orders; some supply-timeline extensions were granted.

qa_highlights.question: What is ethanol capacity utilisation and what is the order visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management framed it as offtake rather than utilisation: 7.8 crore litres for ESY 2026-27 worth about INR500 crore, or about INR600 crore including by-products. Cycle 1 only; more orders expected later.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exploring a buyback given its low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conserving capital to pay down debt when needed, and the buyback question could be revisited in future.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable EBITDA margins by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol 12-15% long term (recent quarters higher on lower grain prices and better by-product realisation); consumer 8-9%; bulk 5-8% and cyclical.

qa_highlights.question: How much consumer raw material cost increase has been corrected, and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs had already improved sequentially in Q3, with about another quarter needed for margins to normalise.

risks_watch: H2 must deliver about 1.5x H1 revenue and EBITDA to meet guidance; the analyst view is that falling OMC ethanol prices and rising grain costs make this hard.
Consumer division flat at INR40-50 crore quarterly revenue, with Q2 margin well below the 8-9% norm; watch the snacking and popcorn launches and whether volume disclosure starts next quarter.
Ethanol order visibility beyond the cycle 1 tender (7.8 crore litres) depends on C2/C3 tenders; margin depends on grain prices and the mix shift to FCI rice.
Bulk division realisations expected to moderate as commodity prices correct.
Management did not give a full capex or depreciation figure; the Q2 slide did not state the exact cost of the 600 KLPD expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and on the ethanol order book, but defensive on the consumer division's flat sales and Q2 margin squeeze, which it called an aberration. It was evasive on buyback, valuation, Tier 1/Tier 2 split, expansion capex and depreciation, and promised follow-ups.
key_quotes: So, we are still confident of achieving our numbers.
We expect cost pressures to ease and business performance to improve over the coming quarters.
So you are commenting on one quarter. You haven't seen this for the last 50 quarters.

adds.what: Ethanol capacity expansion from 282 KLPD to 600 KLPD (fully operational from about August 2026)
Second ethanol facility started with new commissioning completed (per analyst remark on call; not confirmed by management)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-965 crore reiterated (midpoint ~INR945 crore, implying H2 must deliver ~INR583 crore vs H1 INR362 crore); backed by ethanol capacity going from 282 to 600 KLPD (commissioned, full from Aug 2026) and ~INR494 crore order book plus new ESY order, but consumer and bulk margins are weak and H2 would need ~1.5x H1 profit, so backing is partial.

oneOffs.what: Q2 bulk division growth came from higher realisations on commodity prices, which management expects to moderate as commodity prices correct

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 38.9% YoY to INR204.9 crore while EBITDA rose only 23.2% and margin fell to 9.1%, with the brief attributing growth in bulk to higher realisations that management expects to moderate, and no quantified one-off item or volume growth figure is given for the quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 9.1% vs H1 11.3%; management says input costs normalise in about one more quarter and consumer margin norm is 8-9% from 5.6% in H1 consumer, with ethanol at ~18% margin and 12-15% long-term.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ethanol capacity went from 282 to 600 KLPD (+112.8%), fully operational from about August 2026, so Q3 FY27 reflects it fully; ~INR300 crore capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ethanol offtake of 7.8 crore litres for ESY 2026-27 (about INR500 crore) starts 1 Nov 2026 with ~INR494 crore order book; consumer sales stuck at INR45-50 crore per quarter, so growth is ethanol-led.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capacity beyond the completed 600 KLPD expansion was discussed; management is conserving capital to pay down debt (D/E 0.85x).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-965 crore was only reaffirmed; H1 delivered INR362 crore so H2 must deliver about INR583 crore (~1.6x H1), which makes an upgrade hard.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must carry about 1.5x H1 EBITDA (analyst FY27 EBITDA ~INR105 crore vs H1 INR40.8 crore) while OMC ethanol prices fell about INR3 per litre and grain costs rose.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects snacking, grocery, ready-to-eat popcorn (PIPO) and high-protein launches under Oleev sub-brands within two to three months; ethanol-based consumer product permissions secured but no timeline.

rows.label: ESY cycle 1 ethanol order (7.8 crore litres)
rows.why: ESY order of 7.8 crore litres worth about INR500 crore (about INR600 crore with by-products) runs 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Oct 2027; C2/C3 orders are expected but not yet secured.

rows.label: Consumer input cost normalisation
rows.why: Costs already improved sequentially in Q3 with about another quarter needed to normalise, which would restore consumer margins toward the 8-9% norm from 5.6% in H1.

rows.label: Buyback
rows.why: Management is conserving capital to repay debt when needed and only said the buyback could be revisited in future.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance and the ethanol order book and called the Q2 consumer margin an aberration, but was defensive on flat consumer sales and evasive on buyback, capex figures and depreciation; analysts pressed on the H2 ramp needed (~1.5x H1) and falling OMC ethanol prices.
